sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 6

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 6:1
items.html:
Explains: the reason why the screen of Phase 4 raises reflected light up to Keter, and the screen of Phase 3 up to Hochma, and so on, which is, that the magnitude of the reflected light is according to the measure of the light that could have clothed in Phase 4, had the screen not pushed it back. And it also explains that the ten Sefirot of direct light are from above downward, meaning, that the purer among them is more elevated, whereas the ten Sefirot of reflected light are from below upward, meaning, that the coarser among them is more elevated.

The reflected light divides into Sefirot according to its clothing of the Sefirot of the direct light.
And from what has been explained, you will understand well the measure and magnitude of this reflected light, which is neither less nor more, but exactly the measure of the light which the screen returned backward, meaning, that portion which was fit to extend into Phase 4, had the screen not returned it backward. And it rose upward, and clothed the phases of the upper light, namely, Phase 3, which is called Zeir Anpin, and Phase 2, which is called Bina, and Phase 1, which is called Hochma, and also the root, which is called Keter. For this reason, Phase 4, which divided itself into those same four degrees, upon which the reflected light of itself clothed and became four phases, one above the other, in the vessel of Phase 4 itself, because the light that belonged to it rose and clothed these four degrees. And therefore Phase 4 is considered the root phase for them, called by the name Keter of this reflected light.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 6:2
items.html:
The ten Sefirot of direct light are from above downward, and the ten Sefirot of reflected light are from below upward.
And we now find two phases of ten Sefirot in the emanated being, namely: ten Sefirot from above downward, and ten Sefirot from below upward. For there are ten Sefirot in the upper light, namely: the root, which is called Keter of the upper light. And the four phases drawn from the Keter, of which Phase 1 is called Hochma, and Phase 2 is called Bina, and Phase 3 is called Zeir Anpin (including the six Sefirot, Hesed, Gevura, Tiferet, Netzah, Hod, Yesod), and Phase 4 is Malchut, and their order is from above downward, meaning, from the pure to the coarse, that is, that all that is purer is more important, and the purest of all, namely, the root, is called Keter. And after it, meaning, that which is slightly coarser than Keter, is called Hochma, and so on, until the coarsest of all, which is Malchut, is the lowest of all.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 6:3
items.html:
From below upward means that the coarser is more important.
And there are also second ten Sefirot in the emanated being, which are in reverse order from the ten Sefirot of the upper light mentioned above. And these are the ten Sefirot of the reflected light, that rise from the screen that is in Phase 4, as above, clothing the ten Sefirot of the upper light. And their order is from below upward, meaning, from the coarse to the pure, in which the coarser is first in importance, and all that is purer is lower, which is in reverse order to the ten Sefirot of the upper light.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 6:4
items.html:
The Malchut of the direct light is the Keter of the reflected light.
In such a way, that the coarsest of all, which is Phase 4, is the most important of all, for it is the root of all these ten Sefirot of reflected light, since this entire reflected light is no more than the portion of the light belonging to it alone, which the screen returned backward. And therefore, Phase 4 is discerned as the phase of Keter, meaning root, as is known.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 6:5
items.html:
The Malchut of the reflected light is in the Keter of the direct light.
And Phase 3, which is not as coarse as Phase 4, is discerned as the Sefira of Hochma of the reflected light, meaning, the second in degree to Keter. And Phase 2, which is purer than Phase 3, is discerned as the third degree in level above Keter, namely Bina. And Phase 1, which is even purer than Phase 2, is discerned as the fourth degree in level above Keter, namely the Sefira of Zeir Anpin, which includes the six Sefirot, Hesed, Gevura, Tiferet, Netzah, Hod, Yesod. And the phase of Keter of direct light, purer than all of them, is discerned, with respect to the aforementioned reflected light, only as the phase of Malchut, meaning, the lowest of all in level, since the coarser is always more important, and the purer is always lower, as the degrees extend from the coarse to the pure, and remember this well.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 6:6
items.html:
Malchut includes all ten Sefirot of the reflected light.
And behold, Phase 4 itself, by the power of its reflected light that extends into ten Sefirot, likewise divides itself into ten Sefirot, meaning, into four phases and a Keter, for Phase 4 itself is the Keter of the reflected light, meaning, the root, as above, and the nine Sefirot of the reflected light, which extend and rise from her, are its branches, and it is known that all the branches are included and exist in the root, therefore, in Phase 4 itself, five phases are discerned, namely, Keter and the four phases, which are from below upward.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 6:7
items.html:
The refinement of the screen divides Phase 4 into five phases.
And by this you will understand what we brought above (Part 2, Item 8, beginning "however"), that the magnitude of the reflected light is measured according to the measure of coarseness that is in the screen, that the coarser screen, namely, the screen of Phase 4, reveals a complete structure up to Keter. And the screen of Phase 3, only up to Hochma. And the screen of Phase 2, only up to Bina. And the screen of Phase 1, only up to Zeir Anpin. And a screen that has no coarseness at all, not even from Phase 1, meaning, one similar to the root, reveals no structure of light at all, only the phase of Malchut alone, see there. And with what has been explained, you will understand the matter of the aforementioned refinement in the screen over the five phases mentioned, that this is the matter of the division of Phase 4 itself into the five phases mentioned here, in which it is the way of the screen to rise and become refined, through the parts of these degrees of coarseness that are found in Phase 4, for the reason that will be explained before us.
